lesson.title: Git Rebase and Conflict Resolution
lesson.goal: rebase a feature branch onto main with git and resolve the conflicts

steps.title: Set up repo and check branches
steps.instructions: Initialize a git repo with a main branch and a local feature branch (e.g. feature/login) whose commits change index.js and package.json differently from main. Check out the feature branch and run git branch -a to confirm it has no remote counterpart.

targets.caption: Verify the feature branch is local before rebasing

explanations.topic: Why you should never rebase pushed commits
Checking remote tracking branches with git branch -a
How conflicts happen commit by commit during rebase

hints: Make sure you are working on your feature branch and not main before checking branches.
Run git branch -a in the terminal to list both local and remote branches.
Confirm that your feature branch does not appear under remotes/origin/ so it is safe to rebase.
common_mistakes: Rebasing a branch that has already been pushed and pulled by teammates
Running git branch without -a and missing remote tracking branches

steps.title: Start rebase and inspect conflict status
steps.instructions: From your feature branch, run git rebase main to replay your commits onto the latest main commit. When git stops on a conflict, run git status to see the conflicted file.

targets.caption: Start rebasing the feature branch onto main

explanations.topic: Why git pauses rebase when a commit conflicts

hints: Make sure you are checked out on the feature branch, then specify the target base branch in the rebase command.
Run git rebase main, and after it pauses, run git status.
Look at the Last command done and Next commands to do sections in git status.
common_mistakes: Running git rebase feature/login while on main instead of rebasing onto main from the feature branch
Panicking at the conflict message and running git commit instead of resolving and continuing

steps.title: Resolve first conflict and continue rebase
steps.instructions: Open the conflicted file (index.js in the tutorial), remove the conflict markers, and keep the combined code you want. Stage it with git add, then run git rebase --continue.

targets.caption: Remove the conflict markers and keep the lines you want
Stage the file, then continue the rebase

explanations.topic: Fixing conflicts during rebase vs merge

hints: Search index.js for <<<<<<<, =======, and >>>>>>> markers and delete them while preserving the valid JavaScript code.
After saving index.js, stage it with git add index.js.
Run git rebase --continue instead of git commit to proceed.
common_mistakes: Running git commit instead of git rebase --continue after staging
Running git rebase --continue before staging the resolved file with git add
steps.run_command: git add index.js && git status && git rebase --continue
steps.code: const DEFAULT_USER = "admin"; app.get('/profile', (req, res) => { if (req.body === DEFAULT_USER) { res.send('John Smith, the third'); } else { res.send('User not found'); } }); app.post('/login', (req, res) => { const { username, password } = req.body; if (username === DEFAULT_USER && password === 'pass') { res.send('Login successful'); } else { res.send('Login failed'); } });

steps.title: Save commit message and advance rebase
steps.instructions: Save and close the commit message editor (in Vim: Escape, :wq, Enter) to keep the message. Git applies the commit and pauses at the next conflict, if any.

targets.caption: Write and quit Vim to keep the commit message and continue

explanations.topic: How to exit Vim when editing rebase commit messages
Changing git default editor to VS Code

hints: Git opened Vim so you can edit or confirm the replayed commit message.
Press the Escape key to ensure you are in normal mode.
Type :wq and press Enter to save and quit Vim.
common_mistakes: Deleting all text in the commit message editor, which aborts the commit
Typing :wq while still in insert mode without pressing Escape first

steps.title: Resolve final conflict and verify completion
steps.instructions: Remove the conflict markers in package.json, git add it, run git rebase --continue and save the commit message. Run git status to confirm the rebase finished with a clean working tree.

targets.caption: Resolve the conflicting scripts in package.json

explanations.topic: Checking git status to confirm rebase completion

hints: Open package.json and keep only one valid JSON entry for the check script without conflict markers.
Stage package.json with git add package.json and run git rebase --continue, then close the editor with :wq.
Run git status and look for nothing to commit, working tree clean.
common_mistakes: Leaving a trailing comma or invalid JSON syntax when resolving package.json
Forgetting to check git status to verify you are no longer in a detached or rebasing state
steps.run_command: git add package.json && git rebase --continue && git status

steps.title: Open interactive rebase todo list
steps.instructions: Run git rebase --interactive HEAD~3 to open the todo list for the last three commits. Practice changing pick to edit or squash and reordering lines in git-rebase-todo before closing or aborting.

targets.caption: Start an interactive rebase over the last 3 commits
Change pick to edit or squash, or reorder commits

explanations.topic: What interactive rebase lets you do (edit, squash, reorder)

hints: Use the --interactive flag with HEAD~3 to inspect the most recent three commits.
In the opened git-rebase-todo file, replace pick with edit or squash on a commit line.
If you configured VS Code as your git editor (git config --global core.editor "code --wait"), the todo list opens directly in VS Code.
common_mistakes: Forgetting --wait when configuring VS Code as core.editor, causing git to exit immediately without waiting for edits
Deleting a commit line when you meant to squash it, which drops the commit completely
